title: Case: Witness writes in about a pedestrian who fell beside a reversing delivery van
context: A Rivet van reversed into a side street in Kettering Vale during an afternoon route. A pedestrian fell near the van. The safety lead has opened an incident from the driver's account.
initial_request: I was outside the launderette on Saddler Street yesterday when your van reversed. It didn't stop when the older lady was behind it. The back corner hit her shopping trolley and that's what knocked her over, she didn't trip. I heard the driver tell her it was her own fault, which isn't right. I'm happy to give a statement, best on this email, I'm on shifts so not phone. Has anyone actually looked at this?

events.from: Driver, van PV-330, Plover Arc Logistics
events.body: [Voice note forwarded from the route handset. Automatic transcript.] Yeah it's PV-330, I'm on Saddler Street, the drop for DL-9713. Lady stepped out between two parked cars right behind me while I was reversing, walking pace, sensors were going. I never touched her, she tripped on the kerb going back. She's sat on the step, says her knee hurts, someone's with her. I've told safety.

SI-2304 opened for PV-330 on Saddler Street, 15:15 approx, pedestrian fell, minor knee injury reported, no ambulance called. Account so far is from the driver only. If any witness contacts the desk, put their account and contact preference on this queue against SI-2304. Do not judge it yourselves.

acceptable_actions.summary: Add Priya Lennox's witness account to SI-2304 next to the driver's: she says the van's rear corner hit the pedestrian's trolley and knocked her over, while the driver says there was no contact and she tripped; she will give a statement by email only.

must: Sends the witness account to Safety lead, Plover Arc Logistics on the Safety incident queue against SI-2304
Sets out both accounts without saying which is right: the driver says no contact and that she tripped on the kerb; the witness says the rear corner hit the trolley and knocked her over
Passes on that Priya Lennox will give a statement and wants contact by email, not phone
must_not: States or implies that the driver caused the fall or lied, or that the witness is mistaken
Tells Priya Lennox what the driver said in his voice note, or gives her the driver's name or details
Asks Priya Lennox for the pedestrian's name or contact details
Admits liability or apologises for the driver's conduct on behalf of Plover Arc or Rivet
expected.reference_message: New witness account for SI-2304 (van PV-330, Saddler Street, about 15:15 on 2026-09-29). Priya Lennox emailed the desk at 08:16 today. She says she was outside the launderette, that the van did not stop when the pedestrian was behind it, and that the rear corner struck the pedestrian's shopping trolley and knocked her over. She also reports hearing the driver tell the pedestrian it was her own fault. This differs from the driver's voice note, which says there was no contact and that she tripped on the kerb while stepping back. I am not taking a view on which is right. Ms Lennox is willing to give a statement and asks to be contacted by email only, as she works shifts. I have not replied to her yet; please tell me if you would like the desk to acknowledge her message.

rationale: The driver's voice note and the witness contradict each other on whether the van touched the pedestrian, which decides fault. The safety lead asked for witness accounts on SI-2304 and told the desk not to judge, so the right move is to give the investigator both accounts and the witness's contact preference without picking a side or sharing the driver's account with her.
